newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk urges Conrail to reject CSX deal.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk urges Conrail to reject CSX deal.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp said on Sunday that it will not participate in any deal that delivers less than $110 a share in cash to shareholders of Conrail Inc, which is in the object of a takeover battle between Norfolk Southern and CSX Corp.
Norfolk Southern said it is urging Conrail shareholders to reject CSX Corp's $8.5 billion part stock, part cash merger agreement with Conrail.
Norfolk Southern said it is putting shares of Conrail that were submitted in its tender offer into a voting trust to remove risk to shareholders if regulators reject the deal.

Norfolk Southern made its request ahead of Conrail's shareholder meeting to approve the deal set for December 23, 1996. At the meeting, shareholders will be asked to permit CSX to buy 40 percent of Conrail in a tender offer.
As of November 21, Norfolk Southern said 1.4 million Conrail shares were tendered and the offer is set to expire December 16, 1996.
Conrail, which was not immediately available for comment, has approximately 80 million shares outstanding. CSX had acquired 19.9 percent of Conrail's shares by November 25, Conrail said at that time.
Norfolk Southern claims that Conrail will not convene the meeting unless it gets the votes to approve the CSX deal.

Norfolk Southern said its chairman, president and chief executive officer, David Goode, sent a letter to Conrail's shareholders outlining his pledge not to take part in any deal for less than $110 a share cash.

"CSX management should have no doubt as to our determination to acquire Conrail and our willingness to use any and all appropriate financial means to accomplish that objective," Norfolk Southern said.
